title: Grading a model that is never wrong
hook: The model always knows the truth. The answer key does not. What score does it get?

knows: that a model is graded on a test set with an answer key
doesNotKnow: that wrong labels in the key cap the score even a perfect model can get
that near that cap, remaining 'errors' may be the key's

objective: The learner can say that a measured score is agreement with the labels, so if a share of the key is wrong, a never-wrong model scores at most 100% minus that share.

claims.text: The test set and the never-wrong model are a toy: exactly the stated share of the 100 key labels is wrong. Labelled 'Toy test set · model never wrong' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 46 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md, adapted to an exact count of flips (the brief's random 20% gives 80.0% on average over 100,000 draws). MODEL block in Demo.tsx; flipped items chosen by mulberry32(seed 1), untuned; which items are flipped does not change any number.

claims.text: With 20 of 100 key labels wrong, a model that always gives the true answer scores 80%, and all 20 of its 'misses' are the key's mistakes; with 40 wrong it scores 60%.
claims.source: scoreAt(noise) = 100 − noise in Demo.tsx (the model disagrees with the key exactly where the key is wrong). node re-run: 100, 90, 80, 70, 60 for 0..40%.

claims.text: Real benchmark test sets contain some wrong labels.
claims.source: About real systems: Northcutt, Athalye & Mueller 2021, 'Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks', NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks (estimated an average of at least 3.3% label errors across 10 common test sets). The toy's 20% is invented and much higher.

recall.question: About 5% of a benchmark's test labels are wrong. Two models score 94.6% and 95.1%. What should you conclude?
options: Both are near the ceiling the noisy key allows, so the gap may reflect the key rather than the models
Neither model can be any good
recall.why: If 5% of the key is wrong, even a perfect model scores about 95%. Near that ceiling, some of the remaining 'errors' are the key's, so a half-point gap says little.
